ideas: What you learned and who taught you
How you practised and your early mistakes
Why it's been useful in your life

phrases.meaning: an ability useful in daily life

model: Something I learned outside of school is cooking, which I picked up mostly from my grandmother and partly from YouTube. When I was a child, I used to spend every summer at my grandparents' house in the countryside. My grandmother would wake up early to go to the market, and I'd follow her around the kitchen all morning. I didn't really cook back then, but I learned a lot just by watching others, like how she tasted everything and adjusted the fish sauce. When I moved to Hanoi for university, I no longer had anyone to cook for me, so I had to learn properly. At first I used to follow recipes online very carefully, and I still burned quite a lot of rice and ruined a few omelettes. Over time, though, I got more confident, and now I can make most Vietnamese dishes from memory, including my grandmother's caramelised pork. I'd say I'm pretty much self-taught, because nobody ever sat me down and gave me lessons. It's turned out to be a really important life skill. I save a lot of money by not eating out every day, and I eat much more healthily. It also comes in handy socially, because my friends often come over for dinner. Whenever I cook one of her dishes, I feel a bit closer to my grandmother, which makes it even more special.
